subject: On-prem deployment: license scope & evidence schedule
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.ra@medigon.com>
To: hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@medigon.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem deployment: license scope & evidence schedule

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We're preparing internal approval materials for the on-prem deployment and Legal asked us to get a clearer statement from Redwood on two things before our procurement committee signs off:

1) License scope: whether the MSA/order form language permits us to run the service across our staging and DR clusters (we are explicit about production vs non-production).
2) Evidence schedule: a short, auditable package that demonstrates the deployment rights and runtime custody controls (SOC2 artifacts, KMS handling, deployment checklist).

I attached our initial redlines — you'll see we asked for a longer audit window and an explicit KMS handback trigger. Can you confirm what you can provide and a realistic delivery date?

High-level ask: can Redwood provide an "evidence package" and a concrete timeline (3–4 week target) so we can move to procurement?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of IT Operations | Medigon Health
(sanjay.ra@medigon.com)

Attachment: medigon_draft_redlines.pdf

From: hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.ra@medigon.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: license scope & evidence schedule

Hi Sanjay — appreciate the clear ask and the redlines. Quick responses below and a proposed next step: 30-minute touch to align on the checklist and KMS expectations.

- License scope: our standard MSA covers production and non-production uses, but some customers prefer explicit language for on-prem deployments. We can offer two options on the Order Form: (A) explicit non-production carve-out included; or (B) single-site license with an attachable staging entitlement. I'll have legal draft text for both.
- Evidence package: Redwood can provide a bundle of items: SOC2 summary, deployment checklist, runbook excerpt, and a KMS handling statement. We typically do not hand over root keys, but we document key custody and HSM/KMS integration patterns.

Proposed timeline: legal redlines and evidence checklist by EOD Thu (15 Jan). Delivery of packaged artifacts (PDF + drive folder) by Tue (20 Jan) if no further redlines.

Looping in Lauren from Legal to propose specific MSA/Order Form language — Lauren, can you take point on the two license options and the audit window language? Marcus, can you prepare the staging runbook template and a short ops checklist we can attach?

Thanks,
Hiro Tanaka
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
(hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai)

Attachment: redwood_deployment_evidence_checklist.pdf

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.ra@medigon.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: license scope & evidence schedule

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks for sharing the redlines. I reviewed the MSA excerpt and prepared suggested language. High points:

- License scope: replace the generic "deployment rights" clause with: "Customer may deploy and operate the Software in Customer-controlled production, pre-production (staging), and disaster recovery environments within the Territory provided such environments are used solely for Customer's internal business purposes and comply with the Security Addendum." This keeps the scope broad enough for staging/DR while giving Redwood the right to enforce the Security Addendum.

- Audit window: propose a mutual audit trigger limited to once per 12 months with 30 days' advance notice for on-prem evidentiary reviews (not for general SOC2 audits). For urgent incidents the parties may agree to a time-limited forensic review.

- KMS/custody: we should decline any clause that requires handback of private root keys. Instead propose a custody attestation: "Vendor will provide documented key management processes, KMS integration diagrams, and test evidence demonstrating that Vendor does not retain private keys used solely for Customer encryption, or explain the operational constraints if hardware escrow is requested."

I've attached an excerpt with tracked changes and inline comments. Sanjay — if you can highlight any provision you cannot accept, we can iterate quickly.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
(lauren.bishop@redwood.ai)

Attachment: msa_redlines_excerpt.pdf

From: Emma Wilson <emma@wilsonpark.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.ra@medigon.com>, Procurement <procure@medigon.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment: license scope & evidence schedule

Hi Lauren and team,

Representing Medigon's legal — thanks for the quick turn. A few counterpoints from our side (high level):

1) Audit cadence: once per 12 months is reasonable, but Procurement wants a guaranteed 45-day window to complete a remediation verification following any audit findings.
2) KMS: Medigon's security policy requires a contractual path to escrow-like key recovery for governed sites; they are not asking Redwood to hand over vendor root keys, but rather a secure process that allows key restoration in a disaster to customer-controlled HSMs under tightly-scoped conditions.

I've attached a short proposed clause that aims to reflect the above. We'd also like to see the staging_runbook and the specific evidence items you plan to deliver. Can you confirm what format the evidence will take (PDF, signed attestation, or signed statement) and whether Redwood will sign an evidence attestation?

Best,
Emma Wilson
Counsel, Wilson & Park (on behalf of Medigon)
Attachment: proposed_kms_clause.docx

Emma / Sanjay — appreciate the specificity. A few operational concessions and concrete deliverables from Redwood:

- Staging & DR language: we can accept the proposed Order Form addendum text that explicitly lists staging and DR as permitted environments so long as they are Customer-controlled and the Security Addendum applies.
- Audit / remediation: agree to one annual on-prem evidentiary review with a 45-day remediation verification window. For urgent incidents we will cooperate on a limited forensic review with mutually agreed scope.
- KMS path: we cannot hand over vendor master keys. However, we will provide a signed custody attestation, KMS integration diagrams, and an optional key-recovery playbook that outlines a secure, auditable process to restore Customer keys into Customer-controlled HSMs under multi-party approval (Redwood + Customer Security + external escrow custodian). If Medigon subscribes to our Dedicated+ support tier we can include an assigned escrow custodian engagement as a priced line item.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Draft Order Form addendum and redline provided by EOD Mon (19 Jan).
- Evidence bundle (signed attestation, SOC2 summary, runbook excerpt, KMS diagrams) delivered Tue (20 Jan) to the shared drive link.
- Optional kickoff call with Medigon Security to walk through the runbook: propose Wed 21 Jan 10:00am PT.

If that all looks good I'll share the staged artifacts and the DocuSign room link for the Order Form addendum.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
(marcus.lin@redwood.ai)
